svg.title: TYPE_MOVE_AGV -> ExpandAgvMoveJob()
svg.desc: Two MOVE_AGV jobs in one request. An empty AGV produces an AgvMove; an AGV that is carrying a tray produces a TrayMove whose AGV is already fixed.
svg.metadata: ["Start: the request arrives. The map is working_state as the method first sees it; no events yet. Step through the method one table row at a time.", "Row 1. Make a scratch copy of the request's garage and apply every event already in the DAG, so the method sees the garage as earlier jobs will leave it. A replay that fails fails the job. In this example: Job 0: empty DAG. Job 1: replays event 1, so AGV-1 is already at W13. (replay)", "Row 2. Look the AGV up in the scratch garage; a missing or disabled AGV cannot be moved. In this example: AGV-1 and AGV-2 exist and are enabled. (passes)", "Row 3. If the AGV already stands at the destination pose, succeed without adding anything. In this example: Neither AGV is at its destination. (no early exit)", "Row 4. An AGV carrying a tray moves the tray with it: the destination is converted to the tray's heading, a tray with a car takes the node's retrieval heading, and the AGV's destination follows the tray. In this example: Job 0: AGV-1 is empty, so agv_dest = dest. Job 1: AGV-2 carries T9, which has no car, so no retrieval heading applies and both keep heading 90. (dest set)", "Row 5. Check that the AGV's destination exists in the graph and is not kept out for its footprint (empty or carrying a tray). In this example: The footprint depends on whether the AGV carries a tray. W13 and P24 are enabled. (passes)", "Row 6. An AGV without a tray gets one AgvMove, chained after the AGV's previous event (rule A). In this example: Job 0: AGV-1 is empty. AGV-1 has no earlier event, so rule A adds no edge. (adds 1)", "Row 7. An AGV carrying a tray gets a TrayMove with this AGV already assigned, chained after the tray's previous event (rule A). In this example: Job 1: AGV-2 carries T9, so the event is a TrayMove with its AGV already set. (adds 2)", "Row 8. Make the new event wait for any earlier events of the same job (rule B). In this example: Each job has only one event: no rule B edge. (no edge)", "Playing the plan (one illustrative execution: AGV assignment and motion planning choose the real AGV and route): event 1. AGV-1 drives W26 -> W25 -> W22 -> W18 -> W13.", "Playing the plan: event 2. AGV-2 carries T9 W18 -> W22 -> P23 -> P24 and lowers it. No approach drive: T9 was already on AGV-2. Every tray and AGV is now where the plan leaves it."]
